title: Blended Autoscaler Handoff Analysis and Tuning for Probe Noise
creator: Carlos Rivera
description:
Summary: During a regional capacity event on 2026-02-18 we observed a spike of unnecessary scale-ups followed by rapid scale-downs on several Dedicated clusters. The pattern correlated with noisy readiness probe evictions and percentile-based KEDA triggers interacting poorly with HPA smoothing. This ticket documents the investigation, confirms the root causes, and captures mitigations and follow-ups for production hardening.

Scope: Affected services were inference-proxy pools in us-west-2 serving small-sequence chat workloads. Impact manifested as elevated token latency (p50->p95 increases) and increased preemptible GPU churn for customers on Dedicated plans. No customer data loss; some requests hit fallback model variants during spikes.

Objective: Produce a reproducible diagnosis, propose a conservative immediate mitigation to prevent oscillation, and define long-term tuning and telemetry changes so autoscale decisions are resilient to probe noise and bursty cold-start traffic.

root_cause: Primary: An aggressive KEDA percentile trigger introduced earlier (ENG-131002) reduced required observation windows for scaling decisions. This increased sensitivity to short-lived probe-induced CPU spikes. Secondary: readiness probe configuration had no backoff and would transiently fail on warm-pool handoffs, causing repeated container evictions and churn. Tertiary: HPA smoothing/window parameters were tightened by a separate change, making HPA unable to mask short KEDA-driven signals. The combined changes produced positive feedback loops: probe failure -> container restart -> cold cache -> CPU spike -> KEDA trigger -> HPA scale-up -> rapid scale-down as load subsided, causing oscillation.
mitigation:
Immediate: Rolled back KEDA percentile configuration to pre-ENG-131002 values for Dedicated inference-proxy pools and applied a 60s readiness probe backoff setting (probe_failure_backoff=60s) plus a 90s KEDA cooldown override.
Short-term: Add a guard in the autoscaler controller to require two consecutive KEDA percentile breaches across disjoint windows (e.g., both 60s and 300s windows) before scaling above baseline.
Long-term: Implement blended-decider logic that biases HPA decisions when KEDA signals are close to threshold, and add explicit warm-pool awareness so a warm handoff suppresses scale decisions for 120s. Also add configuration templates and a playbook for Dedicated deployments.
action_items: A1: Update runtime to include readiness probe backoff default for inference-proxy (PR #3456) - owner: Maya - due: 2026-03-05
A2: Revert aggressive KEDA percentile change for Dedicated by policy and add staged rollout gating - owner: Priya Shah - due: 2026-03-01
A3: Implement dual-window KEDA confirmation (60s + 300s) to avoid single-window false positives - owner: Platform Autoscale Team (ENG-131002 owners) - due: 2026-03-18
A4: Add HPA smoothing safeguard when KEDA suggests >30% delta vs HPA estimate (suppress scale-up for 90s) - owner: Victor Nguyen - due: 2026-03-15
A5: Create warm-pool handshake signal in control plane to suppress autoscale during handoffs - owner: SRE Team - due: 2026-04-01
A6: Extend observability: add 'probe_evictions' as a first-class metric and surface as alertable anomaly - owner: Observability - due: 2026-03-10
A7: Run chaos test suite with injected probe flaps in staging weekly for 6 weeks and document results - owner: Test Engineering - due: 2026-04-15
A8: Postmortem review with PM/Design/Support and update runbook and customer communication templates - owner: Carlos - due: 2026-03-08
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Decision: Prefer conservative immediate mitigation (backoff + cooldown) over a full revert of HPA smoothing to avoid capacity underprovisioning. Tradeoff: short-term slightly slower scale-up for some bursty legitimate traffic versus reduced oscillation and customer-visible latency spikes. We accepted delaying the dual-window KEDA change to allow more integration testing in staging because it touches multiple clusters and could affect cost projections.

communication_plan: Drafted customer-facing note template for impacted Dedicated customers explaining transient latency and mitigations. Slack incident-summary pinned in #oncall-incidents. Prepare Exec summary for leadership by 2026-03-03. If similar pattern recurs after A1/A2, notify customers within 4 hours and trigger targeted capacity reservations.
notes:
Replay testing in staging replicated oscillation when probe flaps were injected at 8-12s intervals. Increasing probe backoff to >=45s eliminated the false positive cascade in >95% of replays. Cost simulations show a ~1.7% increase in peak reserved GPU minutes if we keep a longer warm suppression window; decision will be re-evaluated at the release planning meeting.
Open question: whether to make dual-window confirmation configurable per-customer (Dedicated vs Hosted). Engineering leans to keep as a platform default with override flags for high-throughput enterprise tenants.
